title: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys used to backdoor WordPress sites
description: A threat actor breached TeamUpdraft's infrastructure, compromising UpdraftCentral connection keys used to manage WordPress sites remotely. These stolen keys have been used to backdoor connected WordPress sites by installing malicious plugins that grant attackers administrator privileges. The breach affects an estimated 10% of UpdraftPlus users with UpdraftCentral or Migrator keys, potentially impacting around 400,000 websites. The vendor responded by revoking affected keys and releasing patched versions of UpdraftPlus. Users are advised to update to the latest versions and remove existing UpdraftCentral keys from their sites to mitigate risk.
aiSummary: TeamUpdraft, developer of popular WordPress plugins including UpdraftPlus and UpdraftCentral, suffered an unauthorized access incident that exposed customer databases and connection keys for UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault, and UpdraftClone services. Attackers used stolen UpdraftCentral keys to send signed commands to connected WordPress sites, installing backdoor plugins disguised as maintenance tools. These backdoors enable arbitrary code execution and creation of administrator accounts. The attack campaign began on October 18, 2026. Initial patches intended to remove UpdraftCentral Cloud keys were incomplete due to a bug, but subsequent updates (UpdraftPlus 1.26.13 / 2.26.13 and later) address the issue. Users must also manually delete UpdraftCentral keys from their WordPress settings to fully mitigate the threat.
aiImpact: The compromise allows attackers to remotely execute arbitrary code and create privileged administrator accounts on WordPress sites connected via UpdraftCentral. This results in full site takeover capabilities, including the installation of persistent backdoor plugins. Approximately 400,000 websites are potentially exposed due to the widespread use of UpdraftCentral keys. The breach also exposed customer data such as password hashes and two-factor authentication settings, though no payment information was stored. The attack does not exploit vulnerabilities in WordPress or UpdraftPlus directly but leverages stolen valid credentials to bypass security controls.
